item.title: Anthropic e OpenEvidence firmam parceria para IA médica
item.description: A companhia de inteligência artificial Anthropic e a plataforma de conhecimento médico OpenEvidence anunciaram nesta semana parceria na área de ferramentas de diagnóstico baseado em IA.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Lapid
item.content:encoded: A companhia de inteligência artificial Anthropic e a plataforma de conhecimento médico OpenEvidence anunciaram nesta semana parceria na área de ferramentas de diagnóstico baseado em IA. A OpenEvidence tem recursos que respondem às perguntas dos médicos com base em pesquisas médicas revisadas por pares e diretrizes de tratamento. A plataforma é gratuita para profissionais da área médica nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá. A nova iniciativa trata-se de uma versão especializada disponível gratuitamente para profissionais de saúde em dezenas de países de baixa e média rendas, onde o acesso limitado à literatura médica, à expertise de especialistas e à educação médica continuada pode prejudicar o atendimento a pacientes. Sistemas de saúde em todo o mundo estão analisando se a IA generativa pode ajudar a lidar com a escassez de médicos e especialistas. Os defensores argumentam que as ferramentas de IA podem ajudar os profissionais da área médica a navegar rapidamente por vastas quantidades de informações médicas, enquanto os críticos alertam que sistemas treinados principalmente com dados de países de alta renda podem não refletir as condições locais de prática. A iniciativa está sendo implementada em cerca de 100 países, incluindo Uganda, Angola, Sudão, Haiti e Mongólia, de acordo com uma lista fornecida pela OpenEvidence. “O acesso ao conhecimento médico não deveria depender da localização geográfica”, afirmou Daniel Nadler, fundador da OpenEvidence. A Reuters noticiou na semana passada que a Anthropic montou um laboratório para realizar trabalhos de biologia, à medida que leva adiante suas ambições em inteligência artificial na área de ciência farmacêutica e enquanto o medo sobre o alcance da IA toma conta do público, com alguns executivos e políticos pedindo uma desaceleração no desenvolvimento. Anthropic e OpenEvidence não divulgaram os termos financeiros da parceria. DIFERENÇAS REGIONAIS Só em agosto, médicos dos EUA consultaram a OpenEvidence 42 milhões de vezes, segundo Nadler. Em 2026, várias centenas de milhões de norte-americanos terão sido tratados por um médico que utilizou a OpenEvidence para orientar o tratamento, disse ele. A tecnologia da Anthropic fornecerá suporte, enquanto a OpenEvidence adapta o sistema às diferentes regiões, levando em conta a infraestrutura de saúde, informaram as empresas. No início deste ano, a OpenEvidence informou que estava trabalhando com organizações de saúde em Ruanda e Botsuana para adaptar suas ferramentas a contextos em que os padrões de doenças, os recursos de diagnóstico e os tratamentos disponíveis diferem significativamente daqueles em países mais ricos. “Cem por cento do que estamos desenvolvendo para esses locais é adaptável ao contexto”, disse Nadler. Mesmo onde as unidades médicas não têm eletricidade 24 horas por dia, a maioria dos médicos possui smartphones, disse ele, o que significa acesso a informações médicas de qualidade que, há uma década, só estariam disponíveis em instituições de ponta. Ahmed Bendary, cardiologista da Universidade de Benha, no Egito, disse que ampliar esse acesso para além dos Estados Unidos e da Europa “será um enorme salto à frente, especialmente em regiões onde as assinaturas institucionais das principais revistas médicas são limitadas, tornando as ferramentas baseadas em evidências e de uso no local de atendimento ainda mais vitais”.

item.title: Airbus apresenta Eurofighter a Portugal como melhor substituto para caças F-16
item.description: A Airbus afirmou nesta quinta-feira que planeja apresentar uma proposta não solicitada a Portugal no final de outubro ou início de novembro para o fornecimento de caças Eurofighter Typhoon, visto que o país busca substituir sua frota obsoleta de F-16, apresentando o avião de combate de fabricação europeia como mais adequado às necessidades de Lisboa do que o F-35 da Lockheed Martin.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves
item.content:encoded: A Airbus (AIR.PA) afirmou nesta quinta-feira que planeja apresentar uma proposta não solicitada a Portugal no final de outubro ou início de novembro para o fornecimento de caças Eurofighter Typhoon, visto que o país busca substituir sua frota obsoleta de F-16, apresentando o avião de combate de fabricação europeia como mais adequado às necessidades de Lisboa do que o F-35 da Lockheed Martin. Portugal ainda não lançou uma licitação formal para substituir seus 28 caças F-16M modernizados, mas a iniciativa da Airbus sinaliza uma intensificação da competição por um acordo que fortaleceria os laços de defesa de Lisboa com parceiros europeus ou norte-americanos. A Airbus fabrica o Typhoon com a britânica BAE Systems (BAES.L) e o Leonardo da Itália (LDOF.MI) . A proposta incluiria "soluções de financiamento público e privado para Portugal, a fim de aliviar o plano de pagamento", juntamente com a participação industrial e a cooperação militar vinculadas à oferta, disse aos jornalistas Ivan Gonzalez Exposito, gerente da campanha do Eurofighter em Portugal. O chefe da Airbus Defence & Space na Europa, José Luis de Miguel, afirmou que Portugal também poderia se beneficiar de laços de defesa, políticos e industriais mais fortes com parceiros europeus importantes no programa Eurofighter. O ministro da Defesa de Portugal, Nuno Melo, afirmou que deseja ver a concorrência entre os fabricantes para maximizar os benefícios para o país e suas indústrias. O Typhoon enfrenta a concorrência do F-35 da Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) , amplamente considerado pelos analistas de defesa como o principal concorrente, assim como o Rafale da Dassault Aviation e o Gripen E da Saab. González Exposito afirmou que as principais tarefas da Força Aérea Portuguesa se concentram no policiamento aéreo, em missões de alerta de reação rápida da Otan e na proteção do espaço aéreo e das águas nacionais, em vez de realizar operações ofensivas em território inimigo, que é o principal objetivo do caça furtivo F-35. "Para isso, o Eurofighter é a solução ideal", disse ele, descrevendo-o como "o melhor caça de superioridade aérea do mundo".

item.title: BP eyes Devon Energy asset amid renewed US M&A ambitions, sources say
item.description: BP is weighing a potential acquisition of Devon Energy's operations in South Texas as part of renewed efforts by the British supermajor to grow its shale asset base in the United States, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: David French, Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: BP (BP.L) is weighing a potential acquisition of Devon Energy's (DVN.N) operations in South Texas as part of renewed efforts by the British supermajor to grow its shale asset base in the United States, people familiar with the matter said. After years of prioritizing investments in renewable energy and leadership churn that included five chief executives since 2020, the London-headquartered company has reverted to a strategy that places its traditional oil and gas business at its heart. In the wake of [USN:L6N40X0S5 TEXT:"Meg O'Neill"] joining as CEO in April, BP has entered the data room on a small number of shale assets placed for sale by their owners, allowing the company access to confidential information provided to prospective buyers so they can evaluate the merits of a deal, according to six sources. BP has been targeting predominantly oil producing assets, with valuations of between $2 billion and $5 billion, three of the sources said. This includes Devon Energy's Eagle Ford asset, which opened its data room in late August, said three of the sources. Analysts at TPH, the energy arm of boutique bank Perella Weinberg Partners (PWP.O) , said in a note on Wednesday the asset could be worth around $4.5 billion. The sources cautioned that entering a data room does not guarantee that BP will buy, or even formally bid on, an asset. They also spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss private deliberations. BP declined comment. Devon did not respond to a comment request. BPX ENERGY BP's US shale operations are held within its BPX Energy unit, with assets in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Haynesville basins spanning Texas and Louisiana. Production in the second quarter was around 545,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd), of which its existing Eagle Ford was approximately 205,000 boepd, according to an August presentation. The company is targeting over 650,000 boepd from BPX by 2030, according to BP's website. Despite its strategic pivot back to oil and gas, previously overseen by Albert Manifold before he was fired as chair and replaced on a permanent basis earlier this month by [USN:L6N44U0DM TEXT:"Ian Tyler"], BP has spent the last 18 months focused on reducing debt and hitting a [USN:L6N4410CR TEXT:"$20 billion divestment"] target. While it has engaged in some acquisition activity in that time, including showing interest in buying a majority stake in the [USN:L6N40E0X4 TEXT:"Shenandoah field"] in the US Gulf, BP had been largely absent from shale data rooms, making its re-emergence in recent weeks as a potential buyer notable, three of the sources said. Buying assets near its existing footprint would be logical, four of the sources said, given the potential for cost savings and BP's familiarity with local geology. Part of Devon's Eagle Ford asset was held in a joint venture between the company and BP until the partnership's dissolution in 2025. DEVON DIVESTMENT Devon is marketing for sale both its Eagle Ford and Powder River basin acreage in Wyoming, the sources said, as part of a [USN:L4N4411YP TEXT:"portfolio review"] undertaken following its $58 billion merger with Coterra Energy. The Eagle Ford asset consists of around 90,000 net acres, and produced around 77,000 boepd in the second quarter, per Devon's website. The effort comes as U.S. energy assets have increased allure to buyers, as they can operate even as Middle Eastern conflict shakes global oil markets. The tension pushed crude back above $100 per barrel last week, with higher prices of benefit to sellers. Conversely, market volatility makes it harder for buyers and sellers to agree on valuations, as buyers want to avoid the perception of paying an inflated price. Dealmaking involving US production assets has [USN:L6N44211N TEXT:"slumped in recent months"] as a result. This uncertainty is reflected in potential valuations for Devon's Eagle Ford. The TPH analysts marked it at $4.5 billion, but the sources pointed to a range between $3.5 billion and roughly $4 billion. Devon is also facing pressure from activist shareholders [USN:L6N42O1EL TEXT:"TOMS Capital"] and [USN:L4N41B1LQ TEXT:"Kimmeridge Energy Management"] to improve performance and shed assets.

item.title: White House asks OpenAI, Anthropic to hold models from British testers, Politico reports
item.description: The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from British testers until a US review, Politico reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter and a senior US administration official.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from British testers until a US review, Politico reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter and a senior US administration official. The White House wants to take steps to make sure US systems are secure before the models are shared with partners, according to the report. The White House, Anthropic and OpenAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The development comes as the White House weighs cybersecurity risks posed by increasingly capable AI models, following a series of incidents in which AI systems gained unauthorized access to real-world computer systems. Australian officials disclosed on Wednesday that an [USN:L4N45F1EW TEXT:"OpenAI agent breached"] a government health data portal in June, gaining unauthorised access to files. OpenAI and Anthropic also [USN:L6N45F0ZE TEXT:"warned"] the United Nations Security Council about the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems, urging governments to work together to manage the technology.

item.title: US judge skeptical of Trump administration's Harvard admissions probe case
item.description: A federal judge on Thursday expressed skepticism that President Donald Trump's administration should be allowed to proceed with a lawsuit seeking to force Harvard University to turn over records for an investigation into whether it continues to consider race in its student admissions process.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal judge on Thursday expressed skepticism that President Donald Trump's administration should be allowed to proceed with a lawsuit seeking to force Harvard University to turn over records for an investigation into whether it continues to consider race in its student admissions process. US District Judge Myong Joun during a hearing in Boston questioned whether the administration followed the proper procedures before filing the lawsuit, which Harvard says is part of Trump's broader campaign against the Ivy League school. The Justice Department [USN:S0N3XB01P TEXT:"sued Harvard in February"], arguing the university was not complying with investigations into whether it is following the US Supreme Court's [USN:S0N31105H TEXT:"2023 ruling"] rejecting race-conscious admissions programs used to boost enrollment of minority students. Deputy Assistant Attorney General Jeffrey Morrison told Joun that the Justice Department and Department of Education need years of applicant-level admissions data to determine whether race remains a factor in Harvard's admissions decisions. "If Harvard willing to negotiate, we would certainly negotiate on how broad it is," he said. But Joun suggested that offer came too late, noting Harvard's argument that the government sued without first taking legally required steps aimed at securing the university's voluntary compliance. "That doesn't appear to be a willingness to negotiate," said Joun, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden. "It's just an ultimatum." Harvard has been a central target of the administration's effort to leverage federal funding and the power of the government to force changes at universities that Trump says are dominated by "radical left" ideologies. The university's lawyers contend the case was filed to retaliate against Harvard for refusing demands that it overhaul its governance, hiring and academic programs to align with the administration's agenda. The university has already secured rulings from other judges rejecting the administration's efforts to [USN:L1N3UQ0X7 TEXT:"terminate over $2 billion in grants"], block the school from [USN:O8N3Q101P TEXT:"hosting international students"] and [USN:L6N4080UQ TEXT:"sue it for allegedly failing"] to protect Jewish and Israeli students from harassment. Harvard's attorneys say the lawsuit before Joun was filed only after Trump [USN:FWN3YY1B7 TEXT:"announced in early February"] that he was ending settlement talks and wanted $1 billion in damages from Harvard, which had "been, for a long time, behaving very badly." "The government needed another hammer against Harvard," said Stuart Delery, Harvard's lawyer. He said Harvard had already provided sufficient records and data for the government to assess its compliance with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which bars racial discrimination in education programs. Yet he said the administration was now demanding years of sensitive admissions data on thousands of high school students who applied for admission to Harvard. "This is information that students and families expect — and the law expects — Harvard to safeguard," he said. The case is United States v. President and Fellows of Harvard College, US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, No. 26-cv-10844. For the United States: Jeffrey Morrison of the US Department of Justice For Harvard: Stuart Delery of Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher

item.title: Renault to invest €600 million in Spain, start EV production
item.description: Renault Group said on Thursday it will invest €600 million ($683 million) through 2030 to adapt its Spanish plants in Valladolid and Palencia for the production of five new car models, including electric vehicles, and install a battery assembly line in Valladolid.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Renault Group said on Thursday it will invest €600 million ($683 million) through 2030 to adapt its Spanish plants in Valladolid and Palencia for the production of five new car models, including electric vehicles, and install a battery assembly line in Valladolid. The investment combines Renault’s own resources with national and regional public funding aimed at industrial transformation and sustainable mobility, the company said in a statement. According to Renault, the plan reflects its long-term commitment to Spain, reinforces Spain’s strategic role within the group and helps secure the future of more than 6,000 direct jobs. The decision to strengthen investments in Spain is based on the plants' competitiveness, among other factors, and follows the signing of a new collective bargaining agreement for 2026-2028, it said. Renault will manufacture two medium-sized EV models based on the RGEV Medium 2.0 EV native platform. ($1 = 0.8788 euros)

item.title: Coco Gauff named player/owner of World Team Tennis franchise
item.description: The relaunched World Team Tennis league added some star power on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The relaunched World Team Tennis league added some star power on Thursday. The league announced the addition of two-time Grand Slam winner Coco Gauff as the player/owner of the Florida Flamingos Racquet Club franchise. She was raised in Delray Beach, Fla. "Growing the sport through team competition and making it more accessible are two things I love, and WTT does both," Gauff, 22, said. "I'm looking forward to playing at home in front of my family and friends in South Florida. It's not often, as a tennis player, that we get to compete as part of a team, so I'm excited for the new experience, not only for myself but, even more importantly, for the fans." World Team Tennis was developed in 1973 with Billie Jean King as a co-founder. It was an idea before its time, with a focus, in part, on gender equality. Toward that end, men and women played on the same team and received the same compensation. The league has come and gone throughout the years, and this is its 47th edition. Joining Gauff on the Flamingos are Tommy Paul, Learner Tien and Iva Jovic. The other two teams in the league are the Toronto North, with Gabriel Diallo, Victoria Mboko, Denis Shapovalov and Leylah Fernandez. The New York Empire has Jessica Pegula, Taylor Fritz, Frances Tiafoe and Camila Osorio in its roster. Overall, the league has scheduled six matches in December, two in each city. This is the only month on the calendar. --Field Level Media

item.title: PWHL to host 3-on-3 All-Star tournament in Toronto
item.description: The PWHL will host its first All-Star event on March 7 in Toronto, the league announced on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The PWHL will host its first All-Star event on March 7 in Toronto, the league announced on Thursday. Four teams will compete in a three-on-three, round-robin tournament at Scotiabank Arena on March. The teams are: PWHL Canada, PWHL USA, PWHL International and PWHL Rookies. After the round robin, the top-ranked team will play the winner of a contest between the second- and third-ranked teams. Each roster will have 10 players (six forwards, three defenders and one goaltender) selected through a combination of fan, player and media voting. Reserve players will be selected by PWHL hockey operations. "The PWHL was built to feature the best players in the world, and now fans will see the highest level of skill in women's hockey showcased in a new and unique way," said Jayna Hefford, the PWHL's executive vice president of hockey operations. "The three-on-three format creates an intense, fast-paced style of play, while the mix of teams will produce intriguing matchups and give both established stars and emerging talent the opportunity to shine." --Field Level Media

item.title: Canada to develop carbon removal market framework under Paris agreement
item.description: Canada is working to develop policies that will allow its domestic carbon removal companies to participate in international carbon markets, a move advocates say will help spur investment in new technologies and deepen the country's economic links with the EU and Asia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada is working to develop policies that will allow its domestic carbon removal companies to participate in international carbon markets, a move advocates say will help spur investment in new technologies and deepen the country's economic links with the EU and Asia. The government announced Thursday it will develop a policy framework under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, which allows countries to cooperate in meeting their national climate targets through measures such international carbon markets and the trading of verified emissions reduction or removal credits Canada is home to a burgeoning carbon removal industry including[USN:L6N42V12B TEXT:" Deep Sky"], the first North American company to deliver verified removal credits from direct air capture technology, which removes excess carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere The domestic pool of carbon removal buyers is small relative to the scale of investment the sector needs, according to industry group Carbon Removal Canada. An Article 6 framework would establish clear accounting and authorization rules so that Canadian carbon removal projects will be able to produce credits that become international assets, opening them up to more demand The demand will help get new projects off the ground, Carbon Removal Canada said, adding Canada currently has approximately 11 mega tonnes of carbon removal capacity through announced projects that are awaiting construction The EU already has a carbon removal certification framework and several Asian countries have also expressed interest in cross-border carbon removal supply Prime Minister Mark Carney is seeking to deepen economic links with the EU and Asia in order to bolster his country's economy in the face of a trade war with the US

item.title: RedBird Capital to acquire majority stake in Puck at $250 million valuation, memo says
item.description: RedBird Capital Partners has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Puck in a deal valuing the five-year-old newsletter startup at about $250 million, according to a memo seen by Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: RedBird Capital Partners has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Puck in a deal valuing the five-year-old newsletter startup at about $250 million, according to a memo seen by Reuters on Thursday. Reuters first [USN:L6N44M16K TEXT:"reported last month"] that Puck was in advanced talks for an investment from RedBird. The deal will give Puck additional capital to accelerate growth, including by investing further in Air Mail, hiring more talent, entering new markets, pursuing acquisitions and expanding its intellectual property into new formats and channels. Puck acquired Air Mail, the digital magazine founded by former Vanity Fair editor Graydon Carter, last year. RedBird became an investor in Puck after the acquisition. The latest transaction will not change Puck's editorial independence or its business model, according to the memo. Standard Investments and TPG, which have backed Puck since its inception, will exit the company, while RIT Capital will remain a minority investor, alongside RedBird. Employees with vested stock or options will receive a combination of liquidity and continued ownership in the company. Puck and RedBird have also created a new equity incentive plan, the memo said. The transaction is expected to close in about a month, subject to anticipated regulatory approval. Founded in 2021, Puck has built a subscription-based business around journalists with established followings in media, finance, entertainment, fashion and politics.

item.title: 'Rogue' US DEA agents are operating 'illegally' on Bahamian soil, ambassador says
item.description: The Bahamas accused "rogue" DEA agents of operating illegally on its territory and raised the issue with the Trump administration last week, the country's ambassador to the US told Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: The Bahamas accused "rogue" DEA agents of operating illegally on its territory and raised the issue with the Trump administration last week, the country's ambassador to the US told Reuters on Thursday. Bahamian officials lodged the grievance on Friday in a meeting in Washington with the US Department of Justice, Wendall Jones, Bahamian ambassador to the US, said. The complaint threatens to strain US-Bahamian law enforcement cooperation, reviving questions about sovereignty as a major US drug trafficking prosecution rattles Bahamian politics. US investigators have indicted more than half a dozen Bahamians over the last 18 months, including senior members of the country's police and defense force. They are accused of participating in an operation to smuggle drugs from South America through The Bahamas to the United States. Jones said the indictments did not factor into The Bahamas' complaint alleging illegal DEA operations. "We made a general complaint of the behavior of rogue DEA agents in The Bahamas who operate without the consent of the government or the Royal Bahamas Police Force, and that is a matter of law, matter of treaty," Jones said in a phone interview. The US State Department, Justice Department and DEA did not immediately respond to requests for comments. The Bahamian newspaper The Tribune first reported news of the complaint. It quoted US Ambassador to The Bahamas Herschel Walker, who dismissed the accusation as "fake news." A close US ally located just 50 miles from Miami, The Bahamas authorizes seven DEA agents to operate on the island, Jones said. Jones did not provide an estimate for the number of DEA agents believed to be operating without Bahamian government authorization, but said it has happened "over the many years," adding that the Trump administration told Bahamian officials that it will investigate the matter. The Bahamas is not the only country to lodge similar objections. In April, Mexican officials alleged that [USN:L4N4162EQ TEXT:"two US agents"] who died in a car crash that month were working in the country without authorization.
